title: Traffic Lights, Signals & Authorised Signals
whatItIs: Traffic lights, flashing red lights and signals from authorised people are orders you must obey.

keyFacts.text: You MUST obey traffic lights and signals from police, traffic officers, wardens and DVSA officers.
If the primary signal isn't working, you MUST obey the secondary signal across the junction.
Alternately flashing red lights mean you MUST stop (e.g. level crossings, fire stations).
Advanced stop line: you MUST stop at the first white line if the lights are amber or red.

keyFacts: Lights out of order? Treat it as an unmarked junction.

items.label: Red
items.meaning: Stop. Wait behind the stop line.

items.label: Red and amber
items.meaning: Still stop. Don't go until green shows.

items.label: Green
items.meaning: Go if clear. Give way to pedestrians crossing.

items.label: Amber
items.meaning: Stop, unless past the line or too close to stop safely.

a.label: DVSA officers
points: Can stop vehicles on all roads
Flashing amber lights, front or behind

b.label: Traffic officers
points: Most motorways, some A roads (England and Wales)
Flashing amber lights, usually from behind

onTheTest.question: A green 'ahead' arrow replaces the full green. You want to turn right. What should you do?
options: Turn right if it looks clear
Turn right if no one is behind
onTheTest.why: Know Your Traffic Signs: if the full green is replaced by an ahead or left-turn arrow, wait until the right-turn arrow shows.

onTheTest.question: You've just crossed the first line of an advanced stop line when the lights turn red. What must you do?
onTheTest.why: Rule 178: past the first line when the signal goes red? Stop as soon as possible: you MUST stop at the second white line.

traps: Red and amber together still means STOP.
Green filter arrow: a filter lane only. Don't enter it unless you're going that way.
A green arrow with a red light lets you go, but only in the arrow's direction.
